sections.heading: Roof Repair, Roof Replacement, or New Roof Installation? The 25% Rule and NJ Permits

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: When damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, a full replacement usually makes more sense than another repair. In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months also requires a construction permit on any building other than a detached one- or two-family home, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

c.v: Do I need a permit to replace my roof in NJ?

runs.v: Re-roofing a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit; a roof replacement on a multi-family, attached, or commercial building does. When the existing roof is past repair, a replacement can use shingle or flat roof systems, with EPDM and TPO common for flat roof replacements; Newark Quality Roofing installs GAF and Owens Corning systems, whose manufacturers offer 50-year warranty options, and regular inspections can extend the lifespan of any roof.

faqs.q: How often should I have my Orange roof inspected?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends a roof inspection at least twice per year, spring and fall, plus one after any major weather event; at a minimum, regular roof inspections should occur at least once a year. Proper maintenance on that cadence extends asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA, and tree-shaded Orange blocks benefit most from the post-storm check.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit or historic approval for roof work found during an Orange inspection?

runs.v: A detached one- or two-family home needs no construction permit for re-roofing under the NJ Uniform Construction Code, while other buildings follow the 25% rule above. Properties in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office before work.

faqs.q: Can you inspect a roof I am considering buying in Orange?
